title: The Book I Could Recite
subtitle: Performance of learning versus the safety to learn
sourceCredit: Abigail Ladd · The Moth Radio Hour, “Confidence Game”

shot.title: A fluent-looking page
shot.direction: The child appears confident; keep the real printed words indistinct and the memorized images separate.

illustration.direction: In a modest sunlit reading corner, the child sits firmly in a little wooden chair holding a real open picture book with both hands. Her bright expression and lifted chin perform a familiar ending; a small bounded wash of a fox running home floats well apart from the real pages as a memory image. The adult sits nearby listening, not looming. Actual page marks remain indistinct, with one small blank word space that her finger has not yet reached.

beats.caption: Wonderful. What does this line say?
beats.speaker: ADULT

shot.title: A gentle question
shot.direction: The adult asks about one actual line, pointing under it rather than testing a performance.
shot.soundDirection: Pages rustle and a bright recitation tune quiets into intimate pencil sounds.

illustration.direction: The adult has leaned only enough to place one index finger beneath a short line on the open book, with wrist and elbow visibly continuous and her other hand resting on her own chair. The girl keeps the book supported on her lap, eyes moving from the adult's face to that specific place. The fox memory wash stops at the edge of the cell. Warm curiosity in the adult's face, no raised eyebrow of accusation, no readable printed sentence.

actions.direction: The adult dips toward the actual line before a short finger trace; the child follows the place with a delayed chin dip. Book corners, chair arms and the table remain steady.

shot.title: The smile stops
shot.direction: The imagined story halts first. Her smile follows a moment later.
shot.soundDirection: Pages rustle and a bright recitation tune quiets into intimate pencil sounds.

illustration.direction: The child's smile has fallen to a small uncertain mouth; she looks down at the unfamiliar place and gently grips the lower corners of the book, elbows close to her body. The imagined fox has faded, leaving only the real page and ordinary room. The adult waits with her pointing hand withdrawn, shoulders relaxed and eyes kind. Keep their chairs and the child's grounded feet believable; no tearful spectacle, mocking classmates or shaming gesture.

shot.title: A chair beside her
shot.direction: Move the adult’s chair beside, not opposite, the child.

illustration.direction: The adult has moved her chair beside the child's instead of opposite, both seats solid on the same floor. They share a natural diagonal view of the open book on the child's lap. The adult offers an open hand near, not over, the child's hand and smiles softly; the child looks back with tentative relief. The book stays hers to hold. Leave clear air between their faces and avoid adult hands swallowing small fingers.

beats.caption: That’s all right. We can figure it out together.

actions.direction: The adult makes a low open-hand offer without crossing into the child’s space. Her head settles first; the child inclines toward her a little later. The book stays supported on the lap.

beats.caption: This one starts with a sound I know.
beats.speaker: CHILD

shot.title: A sound she knows
shot.direction: A finger travels under one real word; let the first sound take effort.
shot.soundDirection: Pages rustle and a bright recitation tune quiets into intimate pencil sounds.

illustration.direction: The child traces beneath a single small word area with her own index finger, supported by a relaxed wrist, brow concentrating and lips forming an effortful first sound. Her other hand keeps the book steady. The adult sits beside her with a separate finger nearby but does not move the child's hand or speak for her. Show coherent shoulders, elbows and lap contact; the rest of the page stays quiet and indistinct.

actions.direction: The child bows her head toward the page, then traces a short real word area with her connected hand. The adult follows the child’s pace rather than moving her finger for her.

shot.title: The shared page
shot.direction: Two fingers and one word remain. No magical instantaneous literacy montage.
shot.soundDirection: Pages rustle and a bright recitation tune quiets into intimate pencil sounds.

illustration.direction: A warm slightly wider two-chair composition holds the girl and adult side by side over the same open book. Two distinct fingers rest beneath one little line, each connected to its own visible arm. The child's face has a small thoughtful smile rather than triumphant graduation; the adult's expression says she can stay. Ordinary chair legs, hanging child feet near the floor and a small side table make the scene intimate and stable. No magical swarm of letters or diploma.
